Which one governs a purely narrative detail the player wrote down is the owner's taste, and it recurs across the corpus (any 'name your X' pick with no mechanical consequence).

results.answer: Never add a slot — that would be a straight rules error. RAW: the feat lets you prepare TWO spells in ONE existing slot and 'When you Cast a Spell from that slot, choose which spell to cast. Once you've chosen, the unused spell dissipates as though you hadn't prepared it at all'. Your number of castings is unchanged. Model it as a paired preparation on the chosen slot: record the chosen rank (at least 1 lower than your highest), let the player prepare a second spell into that one slot, show both, and have casting either one consume the single slot. If the paired-preparation UI is too much for now, the fallback is recording the rank plus a note — but the slot COUNT must not move under any implementation.

That is the same reason creation-fixed variants already ship as separate records here (faith-tattoo-greater/major/true, essence-forge-lesser/moderate/greater, awakened-cold-iron-shot). The deity gets NO field: the candle's effect is identical whichever deity it honours, so it changes nothing computed — the same target-side/flavour reasoning as ruling F. General rule to reuse: split into variant records when the variant changes something the engine computes; record nothing when it does not.

results.answer: RAW: they are REPLACED, not added to — the answer is two free items at any level, never four. Perpetual Infusions (7) / Perpetual Potency (11) / Perpetual Perfection (17) are successive upgrades of the SAME two free Quick Alchemy items; Potency and Perfection re-choose the pair at a higher level rather than granting a second pair. So a 17th-level toxicologist shows two 11th-level-or-lower poisons, and the 5th-level picks are gone. In practice this is moot: these are the superseded Core Rulebook (OGL) alchemist features and will not be wired at all (see the perpetual-* answers) — HH ships the Player Core 2 alchemist.

results.answer: Include the 14th option. Ruling H is explicit — 'WHERE THE RULES ARE OPEN, STAY OPEN … Narrowing it would put my ruling on the sheet dressed as the book's' — and the background's own text contemplates it ('you might have been born under a different constellation and gain different benefits as determined by the GM'). Ship 'Other (GM-determined)' as an option that records the pick and carries no grant (EffectChoice options are allowed to have no grant, and the kineticist junction menu already ships that pattern). Because the sign supplies one of the two attribute boosts and the innate spell, pair the option with a free attribute boost and a free-text spell field so the sheet is not left with a boost missing — the rest is the GM's call, said plainly in the option's label.

results.why: Whether Heroes Heaven models sanctification at all is a scope decision about the app, not a rules reading. The rules are clear (holy/unholy is a real trait with real consequences), but the cost is collection-wide — a new Deity field backfilled across ~485 deities, a choice on the cleric `sanctification` feature (which today ships as description-only text with no field anywhere in src/), and a holy/unholy trait concept the strike/damage engine does not have — and the payoff is mostly a tag plus a handful of items. It is also the blocker behind four Faith Tattoo grades, the Taper of Sanctification, Sanctified Relic and the champion/exemplar edges, so answering it once unlocks a cluster.

options.label: Model it — a real build field
options.looksLike: Deity records gain 'Sanctification: holy / unholy / either / none'; a cleric or champion of a deity offering both is asked to choose at build time; the sheet shows a 'Holy' (or 'Unholy') tag beside the deity, items like the Taper and the Faith Tattoos can set it, and holy/unholy-keyed effects can be gated on it. Lurlup gets 'Can be Unholy' as a real, pickable option.

options.label: Leave it narrative
options.looksLike: The deity page keeps printing 'Sanctification: Can be Unholy' as text in the description and nothing else changes. Lurlup needs no choice (needsBuildChoice = false), the Faith Tattoos' self-sanctification clause gets no surface, and holy/unholy stays something the player tracks at the table.

options.label: Record-only middle
options.looksLike: One pick on the cleric/champion sanctification feature ('holy / unholy / none') that shows as a tag on the sheet and is stored, with no deity-side data and nothing gated on it — the same 'record the pick, grant nothing' shape used for kingdom feats.

results.recommend: Option 3, the record-only middle, then option 1 later if holy/unholy-keyed mechanics start mattering. It costs one choice on one class feature instead of a 485-record backfill, it puts the answer on the sheet so items and feats that reference it read sensibly, and it does not fabricate deity data we would then have to verify book by book. What it does NOT do is validate that a given deity may be sanctified that way — which is exactly what the deity field would buy, so revisit it if that starts biting.
results.theme: sanctification: model it as a build field, record it only, or leave it narrative
